title: KV cache + kernel routing failure probe
content:
Quick summary:
- Intermittent correctness glitches when switching attention kernels at runtime + KV cache reuse across requests of varying sequence lengths.
- Triggers appear on bursty inputs mixing short and long contexts (e.g., 64 -> 4096) where cached KV offsets or key-padding decisions are probably inconsistent with new kernel's indexing assumptions.

Repro (local, minimal):
1) Start runtime with debug kernel routing enabled: 
   export RW_DEBUG_KERNEL_ROUTING=1
   ./bin/serve --model-path ./models/llama-70b-q4_0 --port 5050 --enable-kvcache

2) Sequence of requests (script below simulates). Notice the second request gets garbage tokens or out-of-order attention effect.

# repro script (curl-ish pseudocode)
# NOTE: timing matters, replicate burst pattern
for prompt in ("short prompt", "very long prompt repeated..." ):
  curl -sS localhost:5050/generate -d '{"prompt":"'+prompt+'", "max_tokens":8, "stream":false}'

Observed failure modes:
- Model emits repeated tokens mid-way through generation for long prompt that didn't happen when kernel routing disabled.
- Logs show kernel change occurred between prefix and generation but KV cache size computed for old kernel (seen in offsets).
- Occasionally segfault in worker when sequence length expands beyond threshold during in-flight caching (rare, reproducible ~1/50).

Key log snippets (copied from /tmp/serve-debug.log):
[2026-02-16 14:03:22.114] INFO route: selected_kernel=fast-attn-32 seq_policy=auto
[2026-02-16 14:03:22.115] DEBUG kvcache: reuse_offset=8192 computed_for_kernel=legacy-attn
[2026-02-16 14:03:22.115] WARN kvcache: kernel_mismatch_detected, forcing fallback
[2026-02-16 14:03:22.116] ERROR worker: write beyond kv buffer (pos=12288 len=2048 buf_cap=12288)
[2026-02-16 14:03:22.116] TRACE kernel-router: switching_kernel fast-attn-32 -> legacy-attn (decision: cost_hysteresis)

Hypotheses (ordered by my confidence):
1) Kernel-specific KV layout: some kernels expect per-token packed layout (no padding holes) while others use block-aligned KV tables. When runtime switches, the in-memory offsets aren't transformed -> read/write mismatch.
2) Off-by-one in reuse_offset computation when seq_len crosses power-of-two boundaries (we hit 4096->4096 edge with 64->4096).
3) Aging/eviction race: background compaction thread shrinks buffer while main worker still writing, but only when kernel switch is triggered (compaction assumes kernel-invariant size).
4) Quantized model code path interacts with kernel selection (different quant kernels allocate different element sizes) leading to buf_cap mismatch.

Commands I ran (notes inline):
- reproduce with kernel routing forced: 
  ./bin/serve --force-kernel=legacy-attn --enable-kvcache  # no failures (baseline)
  ./bin/serve --force-kernel=fast-attn-32 --enable-kvcache # no failures (baseline)
  => failures only when routing toggles between kernels mid-session

- Added verbose KV dump: (prints offsets/sizes in /tmp/kv-dumps)\  export RW_KV_DUMP=1
  # Check dumps: found mismatch in element_size between dumps taken pre/post switch

- Ran a bisect script that toggles request sizes; recorded point where buf_cap jumps:
  bash tools/kvcache/bisect-seqlen.sh --model llama-70b --start 16 --end 4096 --step 2
  -> observed failure reproducible when crossing 2048 -> 4096 (not at 1024 or 1536)

Instrumenting ideas and quick patches tried: 
- Patch A: when kernel switch is about to occur, force kvcache flush (inconsistent but reduces occurrence):
  in kernel_router.cpp: before switch, kvcache->ensure_compatibility(new_kernel);
  Result: failure rate dropped from ~2% to <0.2% in local stress, but performance hit.

- Patch B: add per-kernel kv metadata header to store element_size + layout_type and validate on reuse.
  Result: prevented crashes, exposed more mismatches (element_size changed from 4 to 2 for q4 kernels).

- Patch C: disable compaction during active writes (mutex around compaction).
  Result: removed segfaults but still see logic-level misreads (garbage tokens).

Small reproducer C++ snippet I used to emulate kernel mismatch quickly (gory):
// pseudo
struct KVBufferHeader { uint32_t element_size; uint32_t layout_mode; uint64_t used; }
if (header.element_size != kernel_expected.element_size) { log_warn("kv element-size mismatch"); /* proceed -> corrupt */ }

Open questions / next actions:
- Is there any canonical place where kernel selection policy should perform a KV re-layout? Or should we keep kernel-invariant metadata at allocation time?
- What's the contract between kernel implementations and KV cache layout? I can't find a writeup. File a short RFC?
- Could a tiny on-the-fly conversion layer be acceptable (slow path): convert cached keys to new layout on kernel switch. Test perf impact.

Tests to run:
- Unit test: create fake kernel A/B with differing element_size and assert ensure_compatibility triggers a full re-layout when mismatch.
- Stress test: long-running worker making randomized seqlen jumps (16/64/512/2048/4096) with routing enabled for 1M requests. Record failure rate, latency impact with Patch A vs Patch B vs baseline.
- Memory-fuzz: instrument allocator to poison newly converted regions to detect stale reads.

Notes to self (TODOs):
- [ ] Draft tiny RFC for kv-cache kernel compatibility contract + suggested metadata header (include element_size, layout_mode, alignment_granularity).
- [ ] Add linear ticket referencing current logs: RED-3412 (linked above).
- [ ] Try on-disk persistent kv format test (simulate restart mid-switch).
- [ ] Sync with Maya re: compaction thread details (she wrote compact code in 2024).

Helpful traces / where to look in codebase:
- serving-runtime/src/kvcache/* (alloc, eviction, header)
- serving-runtime/src/kernel-router/* (policy code + trace logging)
- serving-runtime/src/quant/* (element size decisions)
- tools/profiling/kv-alloc-stats.sh -> shows peaks aligned to kernel switch times

Slack snippets I posted: "seeing sporadic kv buffer overruns when kernel-router flips kernels mid-session; suspect element_size mismatch between qkernel and legacy kernel — patch B reduces crashes but we need a spec" (posted in #serving-runtime on 2026-02-17).

Appendix: quick binary grep I used: 
  # find places that assume kv element size is const
  rg "element_size" -n serving-runtime | sed -n '1,120p'
  rg "layout_mode" -n serving-runtime || true

End-of-note. Keep this as my scratchpad while I work up a reproducible unit test to propose in the PR linked above. If I don't revisit by Mar 1, ping me (Ethan) to follow up.
